::: {.eyebrow .accent-text .about-eyebrow}
Structural Engineer · Researcher · Vancouver, BC
:::

::: {.lede}
I'm a structural engineer and researcher based in Vancouver, Canada. I'm curious about how structures change over time: how corrosion, damage, and the environment slowly alter the way a bridge or a steel gate behaves, and how we can notice those changes early enough to act.
:::

That curiosity has taken me across four countries. I studied civil engineering at Harbin Institute of Technology in China, with an exchange semester at Monash University in Australia. I then moved to UC San Diego, where I earned my M.S. and Ph.D. in structural engineering with Prof. Michael Todd.

At UC San Diego, in a research program supported by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, I studied pitting corrosion on the steel gates of navigation locks.

I simulated it with multiphysics models and machine-learning surrogates, carried its uncertainty through to a reliability analysis of a whole gate, and updated the models with laboratory measurements. As a postdoc, I turned to diagnosing damage across many similar structures.

In 2025, I joined LPI Ingenieurgesellschaft in Hannover, Germany, to look at the same question from the field: bridges in service. There I automated operational modal analysis of long-term monitoring data, studied how temperature shifts the natural frequencies of an intact and a damaged bridge, and helped interpret field measurements for bridge owners.

Teaching and mentoring have been a rewarding part of the journey, from running modal-testing labs to guiding students through their first research projects. You can read more on the [Experience](experience.qmd) page, or browse the [case studies](work.qmd).

## Technical Toolkit

::: {.toolkit-table}
| Area | Methods and Tools |
|:---|:---|
| Structural Monitoring | Operational modal analysis, system identification, signal processing, acoustic emission, distributed fiber-optic sensing |
| Simulation | Finite-element and multiphysics modeling; Abaqus, COMSOL, FEniCSx, SOFiSTiK |
| Machine Learning | PyTorch, TensorFlow, autoencoders, Gaussian processes, surrogate models, normalizing flows, domain adaptation |
| Probabilistic Assessment | Bayesian inference, model updating, Monte Carlo methods, uncertainty quantification, reliability analysis |
| Scientific Computing | Python, MATLAB, Git, LaTeX |
:::
